structured_output.hypothesis: In North Sea plaice, Fulton's condition factor K = 100*W/L^3 computed per length class is unimodal in length: it rises to a maximum at roughly 30 cm (25-35 cm) and then declines at larger sizes.
structured_output.pass_criterion: Using individual plaice with measured length and weight (pooled across surveys, sexes and years, 5-cm length classes from 10 to 60 cm, median K per class with n>=30), the length class with maximum median K lies within 25-35 cm, AND median K in the 50-60 cm classes is at least 3% lower than the peak, AND median K in the 10-15 cm classes is at least 3% lower than the peak.
structured_output.fail_criterion: The class of maximum median K lies outside 25-35 cm, OR K is monotonic (no interior maximum), OR the decline from peak to the 50-60 cm classes is less than 3%.
structured_output.interpretation: Thompson's k = W/L^3 is Fulton's condition factor (scaled by 100 for W in g and L in cm). 'Size at which sexual maturity begins' is read as the stated ~30 cm window (25-35 cm) and is not itself tested against maturity data; maturity stage in the data can be used as a cross-check. Thompson used grouped averages of Atlantic/North Sea plaice; the modern test uses individual-level survey records. Seasonal variation in condition is a confound: stratify by quarter as a robustness check, but the primary test is pooled.

dataset.name: ICES DATRAS (Database of Trawl Surveys)
dataset.publisher: International Council for the Exploration of the Sea (ICES)
dataset.why_it_fits: DATRAS provides downloadable North Sea trawl-survey data (e.g. NS-IBTS, BTS) via web services and downloads. Biological (CA) records for Pleuronectes platessa include length class, individual weight, sex, maturity and age, so K = 100*IndWgt/LngtClass^3 can be computed per length class and compared with maturity.
